summary: Jay L. Garfield works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Ngawang Samten, Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe, and Robert Thurman, holding posts at Hampshire College, Smith College, and the University of Melbourne.

Jay M. Bernstein is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1971–1975). He held posts at the University of Essex (~1975–1996), Vanderbilt University (~1996–2001), and The New School (~2001).

Jay Valentine specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Delaware (1992), Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Kurtis R. Schaeffer.

Jayandra Soni specializes in Indology and philosophy. He completed doctorates at Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University, later serving as a lecturer at the University of Marburg (1991–2012) and holding a post at the University of Innsbruck (~2012).

Jayashree Sathe specializes in Indology and linguistics. She held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, serving as editor in chief (attested 2011) and later as Professor-Editor for the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).

Jaś Elsner works in religious studies and history/archaeology. After degrees at Cambridge and the Courtauld Institute, he held posts at Cambridge, the Courtauld Institute (~1991–1999), Corpus Christi College, Oxford (1999), and the University of Oxford (2014).
Jean Dantinne is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He held a post as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Jean Deloche was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He taught at Suryavarman II High School, directed the Alliance Française of Madras, and held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Filliozat was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He was a professor at EPHE and Collège de France, and directed the EFEO and French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Kellens is a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Liège and University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, later holding posts at Mainz, Liège, and the Collège de France.

Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Amsterdam. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and served as a professor at Leiden University and director of the Kern Institute.

Jean Przyluski was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Henri Hubert and Marcel Mauss, later holding posts at INALCO (1923–1930), EPHE (1926–1944), and the Collège de France (1930–1944).

Jean Rouch studied at École des Ponts ParisTech, École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and the Institut d'ethnologie under Marcel Mauss (~1940–1944). He later held a post at Paris Nanterre University.

Jean-Baptiste Biot was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at École Polytechnique. He served in the French Revolutionary Army and held professorships at École Centrale de Beauvais, the Collège de France, and the Science Faculty of Paris.

Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the École du Louvre and the University of Paris. He served as director (1986–2004) and museum president (~1986–2008) at the Guimet Museum.

Jean-François Lyotard was a philosopher who studied at the University of Paris and Paris Nanterre University. He held academic posts at Paris Nanterre, Paris 8 University (1972–1987), UC Irvine (~1987–1998), and Emory University (~1995–1998).
Jean-François Revel was a philosopher who was educated at the Lycée Jean-Baptiste-Say, the Lycée du Parc (~1941–1943), and the École Normale Supérieure (1943).

Jean-Louis Burnouf was a linguist who studied under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He held posts at Lycée Louis-le-Grand (~1808–1817) and was Chair of Latin Eloquence at the Collège de France (1816–1844).
Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who was educated at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held a post at the CNRS.

Jean-Luc Chevillard specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Culioli, later holding posts as a researcher at the CNRS (~1991) and lecturer at the University of Hamburg (~2012).
